body:
Triage: lands in `domain:spec` (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.form.ts`); rationale: class (a) — the docstring states something **a passing test asserts the opposite of**. `METADATA_FORM_REGISTRY` registers this form under `permission` only, and `metadata-forms-vocabulary.test.ts` pins that deliberately (no `role`, no `profile` key, no locale bundle carrying a `profile` form group). ⇒ A reader of the comment is told the opposite of an enforced fact. `Bug`.

⚠️ **This is not the "in-file prose contradicts in-file truth" shape this seat has been closing** (objectui#8162, objectui#8270), and the difference is what sets the grade: there is a **second artefact in the conflict, and it ships**. The form's `Identity` section description — translated into every locale — still teaches the concept in full: *"Permission Sets stack on top of a Profile to grant additional access. Profiles are the base set assigned 1:1 to each user."* ⇒ One of the two is wrong, and ⭐ **the wrong one may be the one users read**, in four languages.

`priority:p2` on that basis: a stale internal comment is p3 work; a shipped, translated, user-facing description of a possibly-retired concept is not. ⛔ Note the grade is on the *shipped* sentence, not on the docstring — if the ruling turns out to be that `profile` survives as a kind, the section description is correct and this drops to a p3 comment fix.

⛔ **Do not repair this by guessing, and ⛔ do not repair it from the comment.** The card is right that the two readings lead to opposite edits:
- `profile` retired as a metadata **kind** ⇒ the docstring's first sentence goes **and the shipped section description is wrong** and must be rewritten.
- `profile` retired only as a **registry key** while surviving as a kind authors name ⇒ the section description is right, and only the ADR-0090 D2 parenthetical misstates the scope of what was removed.

⇒ Deciding needs **ADR-0090 read against the current `permission` schema**. That reading is the first work item and it is cheap.

The second defect in the same paragraph is unambiguous and needs no ruling: *"The only flags are minimal (ADR-0090 D2 removed the Profile concept) so admins can see and toggle it explicitly"* names no flag and `it` refers to nothing — a purpose clause that outlived the subject it was written for. The form declares **no boolean field at all** today (its sections hold `name`, `label`, `systemPermissions`, `objects`, `fields`, `tabPermissions`, `rowLevelSecurity`). ⇒ That sentence goes either way; it can be fixed without waiting for the ruling.

⚠️ **Translation cost, and it is the reason this must not be a drive-by edit.** PR #16226's zh-CN translation of `permission.sections.identity.description` is deliberately **faithful to the shipped English source**. If the source sentence changes, the **zh-CN, es-ES and ja-JP** leaves all need re-translating in the same change. ⛔ Changing the English and leaving three locales describing the old concept would be strictly worse than today.

⛔ Nothing here is PR #16226's to fix — that PR is bounded to zh-CN leaf values and correctly translated what shipped.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

## The rulings this dispatch carries, verbatim and non-negotiable

⛔ **Do not repair by guessing, and ⛔ do not repair from the comment.** Triage:

> ⛔ **Do not repair this by guessing, and ⛔ do not repair it from the comment.** The card is right that the two readings lead to opposite edits:
> - `profile` retired as a metadata **kind** ⇒ the docstring's first sentence goes **and the shipped section description is wrong** and must be rewritten.
> - `profile` retired only as a **registry key** while surviving as a kind authors name ⇒ the section description is right, and only the ADR-0090 D2 parenthetical misstates the scope of what was removed.
>
> ⇒ 决定 needs **ADR-0090 read against the current `permission` schema**. That reading is the first work item and it is cheap.

⭐ **Why the grade is p2, and what it is on** — triage again:

> ⚠️ **This is not the "in-file prose contradicts in-file truth" shape this seat has been closing** … there is a **second artefact in the conflict, and it ships**. The form's `Identity` section description — translated into every locale — still teaches the concept in full … ⭐ **the wrong one may be the one users read**, in four languages.
> ⛔ Note the grade is on the *shipped* sentence, not on the docstring — if the ruling turns out to be that `profile` survives as a kind, the section description is correct and this drops to a p3 comment fix.

⇒ The **first deliverable is the reading**, not an edit. Write down what ADR-0090 says against the current `permission` schema, with the evidence, and only then choose which of the two edits applies. If the reading is genuinely ambiguous, ⛔ stop and report — do not pick a side to have something to commit.

The card's **second** defect needs no ruling and is unambiguous: the half-edited ADR-0090 D2 sentence with no subject. That one is repairable regardless of how the first reading comes out.

⚠️ If the shipped section description turns out to need rewriting, its **locale bundles** are part of the change. Measure how many and say so; ⛔ do not leave four languages teaching the retired reading while the English is fixed.

## Clause-② `no` — the widening tell that fires on PR #16941 is a false positive, explained here as the checker asks

Added 2026-09-08T17:4xZ by the claiming seat. `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 16941` returns **exit 4**, a **C5** row:

> declares `Clause-②: no` while its diff carries 1 widening tell(s) … `packages/spec/src/security/permission.form.ts:30` (**T2**) … re-declare `yes` **or explain in the claim why this addition does not widen**.

Taking the second route, because the first would be false. ⛔ The declaration stays `no`, ⛔ the checker's spelling is not relaxed, and ⛔ the diff is not reshaped to dodge a heuristic.

### T2's own definition has no referent in this file

T2 is *"a new member of a closed set (`z.enum` / union / an `as const` array) — the accept set gains a value"*. Measured on the PR head `02daeed44`, with a live control so the zeros are readings:

| grep on `permission.form.ts` | hits |
|---|--:|
| `as const` | **0** |
| `z.enum` | **0** |
| `z.union` | **0** |
| `] as` | **0** |
| `defineForm` — positive control | **2** |

There is no closed set in this file for a member to be added to.

### Nothing gained a member either, on any array

| | `origin/main` | PR head |
|---|--:|--:|
| sections (`label: '`) | 4 | **4** |
| fields (`{ field: '`) | 7 | **7** |

### And the line it names is a replacement, not an addition

```
-        'Permission Sets stack on top of a Profile to grant additional access. …'
+        'Permission sets are the only capability container: …'
```

`:30` is the `description:` **property value** on the existing `Identity` section object inside `sections: [ … ]`. The tell matched a `+ '…'` string-literal line and read a replaced property value as a new member of a closed set.

### The direction is mechanically corroborated anyway, by instruments that did not fire

⛔ This is not "trust the declaration". Two ratchets that *would* move on a real widening are green **with no regeneration required**: `check:api-surface` and `check:authorable-surface`, both inside `check:generated` (all 15 artifacts up to date). A new accepted value or a new published key cannot pass those silently — that is what they are for.

⚠️ Stated plainly rather than glossed: with T2 overruled, this pair no longer has the *widening-tell* limb as its compensating control. What replaces it is not this seat's word — it is those two ratchets, plus the syntactic readings above, plus the fact that the checker itself prints on every clean run that **"a tell is not a proof and its absence is not one either"**.

⇒ Filed as **#16943** so the detector can be narrowed rather than carried as folklore. ⛔ This seat did not and will not edit the checker.
